searchText: Re: 1559 what exactly is hoped to be gained by simulations? The problem is that we don't know how humans will behave, not that we don't know what will happen given certain human behaviors. 1559 is pretty simple in terms of the mechanism design IMO and it can be modeled pretty easily once you have assumptions about human behavior. Creating a simulation won't give you any better of an idea of how humans behave though. cc <@332923501079953409> All I really have to say about that this, you may be right. <@486501030046203915> can you consider plugging your simulation into github.com/ethereum/hive? I can certainly consider it! I am not too familiar with Hive so could use more info on what to achieve. Is the idea to have clients interact in this environment, in which case the simulation becomes a shell for their behaviour? Any starting point in the docs that I can replicate? (e.g., is it something like that? https://github.com/ethereum/hive/tree/master/simulators/ethereum/consensus) This is maybe getting ahead of things, but perhaps if we have 1559 live on a testnet, a bug bounty is the best way to get people to break it? One thing that came up on ACD when <@!332923501079953409> gave an update a while back was the risk of the network not being able to handle blocks that stay "200%" (100% of 1559-capacity) full. The only way we'll know that is probably by having someone spam a network with 1559-full blocks for a while I don't think there is anything wrong with making a bug bounty, but i don't expect it to work.

excerpts.author: sky.cactus
excerpts.content: Re: 1559 what exactly is hoped to be gained by simulations?  The problem is that we don't know how humans will behave, not that we don't know what will happen given certain human behaviors.  1559 is pretty simple in terms of the mechanism design IMO and it can be modeled pretty easily once you have assumptions about human behavior.  Creating a simulation won't give you any better of an idea of how humans behave though.
